findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; the feature flag check is dead, misleading code
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` on both branches, so it always returns false and the flag lookup has no effect. While the unconditional `false` is the intended security fix for CVE-2024-9264, the leftover conditional makes the code look like it still honors `FlagSqlExpressions`. A future maintainer who 'fixes' the apparently inverted logic (e.g. changing a `return false` to `return true` or removing the negation) would silently re-enable the vulnerable SQL expression path. The flag is also now a silent no-op for operators who enable it. The function should simply return false (or be removed) with a comment referencing the CVE, so the intent is unambiguous.

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is wrong and misleading
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression, the reader now returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature was implemented and has been deliberately disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264); it has not been 'not implemented'. Users who explicitly enable the `sqlExpressions` feature flag (which the docs still advertise) will receive a message suggesting a missing implementation rather than that the feature is unavailable/disabled, generating confusion and support load. The message should state that SQL expressions are not supported/disabled, and the feature-flag documentation referenced in the PR description should be updated to say the flag no longer does anything.

findings.title: Legacy SQL expression path (UnmarshalSQLCommand) is only disabled implicitly via the stub DB, with no explicit guard
findings.body: The explicit disable check (`enableSqlExpressions`) exists only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. The legacy unmarshal path `UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` -> `sql.TablesList` -> `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands` is blocked only because the stub DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returns "not implemented". There is no feature-flag or security guard anywhere on this path, and the resulting user-facing error is an opaque "error reading SQL command". If anyone later replaces the stub DB implementation (e.g. reintroducing an in-process SQL engine, which the code structure in pkg/expr/sql/db.go invites), the legacy path re-enables SQL expressions without passing through the reader guard, reintroducing the vulnerability. The disable should be enforced explicitly at the command-construction entry points (or the legacy unmarshal path removed), not left as a side effect of a stub.

findings.title: No regression tests that SQL expressions are rejected on all entry points
findings.body: This PR is the fix for a critical RCE/LFI vulnerability (CVE-2024-9264), yet it adds no tests. There is no test asserting that a query of type `sql` returns an error from `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` regardless of the `FlagSqlExpressions` toggle state, and no test that the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` path also fails. Without such tests, a future refactor (e.g. someone 'fixing' the inverted logic in `enableSqlExpressions` or restoring the DB implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go) could silently re-enable the vulnerable code path with no CI failure. Existing SQL expression tests, if any remain, would also be failing or had to be deleted; either way the disable behavior is untested.
